name: Tolerance Stack-Up
blurb: worst-case and statistical sum of a chain of dimensions
intro: Enter the dimensions of a one-dimensional loop with their tolerances and whether each adds to or takes from the result (for example a gap). It returns the worst-case and root-sum-square (RSS) range, which dimension contributes most, and checks the result against your limits.

inputs.label: Result must be at least
inputs.help: Lower limit of the result, e.g. the smallest allowed gap; empty for none.

examples.title: End play of a gear on a shaft

usage: Give dims as a list of {name, nominal, plus, minus, dir}: plus and minus are the tolerance sizes (minus as a positive number), dir '+' if the dimension increases the result and '-' if it decreases it. Optionally lsl and usl limits for the result, and the unit label. It returns nominal and mean result, worst-case, RSS and modified-RSS ranges, pass/fail against the limits, the expected out-of-spec share, and each dimension's percentage contribution. Use it to check a gap, end play or fit that depends on several parts.
sources: Fortini, Dimensioning for Interchangeable Manufacture (worst case and RSS stack-up)
ASME Y14.5 / ASME Y14.5.1 tolerance analysis practice; Bender's 1.5 factor for modified RSS
